Action recommended: Review Azure Copilot agent access settings before 1 August 2026


You’re receiving this notification because you’re associated with one or more Azure tenants that have Azure Copilot enabled.

What's changing

Starting 1 August 2026, Azure Copilot will introduce individual agents with their own General Availability or Public Preview status. The existing Agent mode experience will be replaced with direct access to supported agents.

For tenants that already have Azure Copilot enabled, all Azure Copilot agents, including agents in Public Preview, will be enabled by default.

The tenant-level Azure Copilot access setting will remain the primary control. If Azure Copilot is currently disabled for your tenant, Azure Copilot agents will remain disabled after this change.

Feature availability beginning 1 August 2026

General availability

Observability Agent

Public preview

Deployment Agent

Troubleshooting Agent

Optimization Agent

Resiliency Agent

Migration Agent

Azure Copilot’s chat experience and capabilities are already generally available.

The Deployment Agent, Troubleshooting Agent, Optimization Agent, and Resiliency Agent will be available directly from the Azure Copilot chat experience.

The Observability Agent and Migration Agent will continue to be accessed through their existing experiences in Azure Monitor and Azure Migrate, respectively.

Changes to agent administration

Starting 1 August 2026:

The sign-up process previously used to request access to Azure Copilot agents will no longer be required.

Access will no longer be managed through tenant allowlisting.

Administrators will be able to enable or disable individual agents in the Azure Copilot Admin Center.

 Recommended action


If you want all Azure Copilot agents to be enabled for your tenant, no action is needed.

If you don’t want Azure Copilot agents to be enabled by default:

Before 1 August 2026: Disable Azure Copilot for your tenant. For instructions, see Manage access to Azure Copilot.

On or after 1 August 2026: Review and manage individual agent access settings in the Azure Copilot Admin Center.

 Help and support 


If you have questions about this change, contact the Azure Copilot team at AzureCopilotPMs@microsoft.com.

The Three Levels of Development

LEVEL 1 • INTRAPERSONAL DEVELOPMENT

Leading Self

Leading Teams

*Audience:* Intact teams, cross-functional groups, mentoring cohorts

Leading Systems

10:00 AM to 05:00 PM

Yes







*Objective:* Strengthen the team’s ability to design, scale, troubleshoot

and integrate enterprise-level Playwright automation frameworks.



*Required curriculum:*



*1. Framework Architecture and Design Patterns*



* Enterprise-level framework architecture

* Advanced Page Object and component-based design

* Separation of test, business, service and utility layers

* Reusable and maintainable framework components

* Configuration management and environment handling



*2. Fixtures Mastery*



* Built-in, custom and strongly typed fixtures

* Test-scoped and worker-scoped fixtures

* Fixture dependencies, composition and automatic fixtures

* Authentication, browser context and reusable setup

* Resource initialisation and clean-up strategies



*3. Scalable Project Structure*



* Organising tests, pages, fixtures, utilities, test data and configuration

* Supporting multiple applications, environments and test suites

* Reusable modules and coding standards

* Tagging, test grouping and selective execution

* Maintaining the framework as the test suite grows



*4. Parallel Execution Architecture*



* Workers, fully parallel execution and serial dependencies

* Sharding tests across multiple agents

* Test isolation and management of shared resources

* Preventing test-data and session conflicts

* Optimising execution time without reducing reliability



*5. API–UI Hybrid Framework*



* Using `APIRequestContext` for API testing and test setup

* Creating data through APIs and validating through the UI

* Authentication and token handling

* Combining API and browser workflows in one framework

* Data clean-up and end-to-end validation



*6. Network Interception and Mocking*



* Intercepting, modifying, fulfilling and aborting network requests

* Mocking API responses and external dependencies

* Simulating failures, latency and edge cases

* Request and response validation

* Using mocking to create reliable and controlled tests



*7. Tracing and Advanced Debugging*



* Trace Viewer and trace-on-retry configuration

* Screenshots, videos, logs and failure artefacts

* Debug mode, Playwright Inspector and breakpoints

* Identifying flaky tests and root causes

* Capturing useful diagnostic evidence in CI/CD runs



*8. Retry Strategy Design*



* Global, project-level and test-specific retry configuration

* Designing environment-specific retry policies

* Capturing traces and evidence during retries

* Distinguishing genuine defects from intermittent failures

* Avoiding retries that conceal unstable tests



*9. Test Data Management*



* Test-data factories and dynamic data generation

* Environment-specific and configuration-driven data

* Unique data for parallel execution

* Secure handling of sensitive data and credentials

* Data creation, isolation, clean-up and repeatability



*10. Azure DevOps CI/CD Integration*



* Creating Playwright YAML pipelines

* Scheduled, triggered and regression test runs

* Sharding and execution across parallel agents

* Publishing HTML/JUnit reports and failure artefacts

* Managing variables, secrets and environment configuration

* Structuring pipeline stages and quality gates

* Troubleshooting failed pipeline executions



The programme should include code-along exercises and practical application

throughout, followed by an integrated final-day lab or capstone. Please

recommend a realistic three-day structure and identify anything that should

*Client Requirement Summary — Advanced Playwright + TypeScript Workshop*



*Fixed Delivery Details*



   - Delivery mode: In-person





   - Location: Vikhroli, Mumbai





   - Dates: 7–9 September





   - Time: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM daily





   - Duration: 3 days





   - Batch size: 12–15 learners





   - Schedule and location are fixed; no changes requested.



*Learner Profile*



   - Participants are experienced testers, senior team members, and top

   performers.





   - Teams will attend from Mumbai and Pune locations.





   - They already know Playwright + TypeScript basics through LinkedIn,

   YouTube, and self-learning.





   - Training must be strictly advanced-level, practical, and relevant to

   production automation challenges.



*Proposed Advanced TOC*



   - Scalable Playwright framework architecture and advanced Page

   Object/component patterns





   - Custom fixtures, fixture scopes, authentication, and dependency

   injection





   - Scalable project structure, coding standards, reusable utilities, and

   new-team-member onboarding





   - Parallel execution, workers, sharding, retries, and test isolation





   - API setup and API + UI automation workflows





   - API-driven test data creation, validation, and cleanup





   - Network mocking, request interception, route fulfillment, third-party

   dependency handling, 403 errors, and timeout simulation





   - Advanced debugging with Trace Viewer, screenshots, videos, HTML

   reports, and custom reporters





   - Retry-design strategy, flaky-test analysis, QA risk management, and

   reliability practices





   - CI/CD integration using GitHub Actions or Jenkins: headless execution,

   artifacts, scheduled runs, and report visibility



*Learning Methodology*



   - Short concept-led sessions followed by hands-on practice.





   - Avoid long continuous lecture sessions.





   - Include a 5–15 minute break or informal discussion after every two

   hours to maintain engagement and retention.





   - Use realistic test-automation scenarios, live coding, troubleshooting

   exercises, peer discussion, and guided labs.





   - Focus on learners applying the concepts in a reusable Playwright +

   TypeScript framework.



*Assessments*



   - Day 1: 30-minute pre-assessment to establish current capability and

   tailor facilitation.





   - Day 2: Mid-assessment to measure concept retention and identify

   support areas.





   - Day 3: Final assessment and hands-on lab evaluation.





   - Share an individual/batch scorecard after the program, covering

   assessment performance, participation, strengths, and recommended next

   steps.



*Lab / VM Requirement*



   - Client has requested confirmation on the lab or VM environment for

   hands-on learning.





   - Delivery/faculty to propose the preferred setup:





   - Learner laptops with pre-installed Node.js, VS Code, Git, Playwright,

      and access to the training repository; or





   - Standardized cloud VM/lab environment, if local installations are

      restricted.





   - Lab should include a demo application, APIs, test accounts, test-data

   endpoints, CI/CD sandbox, and exercises for retries, network failures,

   reports, and debugging.



*Pre-Read Requirement*



   - Share pre-read material, setup instructions, and required URLs by 15

   August.





   - Pre-read should include:





   - Environment setup guide





   - Playwright + TypeScript refresher





   - Git/repository access instructions





   - Required software, access, and laptop specifications





   - Brief overview of the advanced workshop use cases



*Faculty Evaluation*



   - Faculty must attend a 30-minute technical evaluation session before

   final confirmation.





   - Evaluation panel: 3 Technical Managers and 1 SPOC.





   - Faculty should be prepared to demonstrate advanced Playwright

   framework knowledge, practical problem-solving, facilitation approach, and

   a sample lab walkthrough.



*Required Faculty / Delivery Inputs*



   - First draft TOC





   - Trainer profile with relevant advanced Playwright + TypeScript and

   corporate-training experience





   - Clear learning outcomes





   - Training methodology and session plan





   - Lab/VM recommendation and prerequisites





   - Assessment approach, scorecard sample, and feedback format





   - Post-session handout/PDF notes or learning material





   - Commercial details for any post-training support



*Expected Learning Outcomes*



By the end of the workshop, learners should be able to:



   - Design and maintain a scalable Playwright + TypeScript automation

   framework.





   - Build reliable UI, API, and integrated end-to-end tests.





   - Manage authentication, test data, fixtures, retries, and parallel

   execution effectively.





   - Diagnose flaky tests and production-like failures using traces,

   reports, network controls, and debugging tools.





   - Run automation reliably through CI/CD pipelines and interpret

   execution artifacts.





   - Apply practical QA risk and test-design strategies to improve

   automation quality.



*Post-Session Support and Follow-Up*



   - Client wants clarity on support for learner queries after the workshop

   and whether it carries additional charges.

   - 2–4 weeks of monitored query support through email or a shared

   - Optional paid mentoring, framework review, or implementation support





   - Recommend a refresher or advanced follow-up program every 3–6 months,

   based on framework adoption and technology updates.





   - Suggested review cadence: quarterly check-in, with formal refresher

   training every 4–6 months.

Java AI Launchpad Program : Trainer profile requirements

Hi Murali,



Greetings from Synergetic India Pvt ltd

Hope doing good!!



We are looking for a trainer who can conduct training on :  Cloud Computing & DevOps/ AI Generative AI & Data Analytics for Engineers



Training Details







  *   Mode: Classroom

  *   Training location: Hyderabad

  *   Start date: ASAP in Aug

  *   Pax: Freshers

  *   Duration: To be Decided

  *   Content: Expecting from trainer (Topics mentioned below)

  *   Trainer Exp required : 4 to 5+ Yrs







Cloud Computing & DevOps



  *   Cloud concepts: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, regions & availability zones, shared responsibility model, and pricing awareness.

  *   Core cloud services (AWS or Azure based on demand): Compute (EC2/App Service), Storage (S3/Blob), Networking (VPC/VNet, Security Groups), and Managed Databases.

  *   Docker: Images, containers, Dockerfile, Docker Compose, and containerizing a full-stack application.

  *   CI/CD using GitHub Actions: Build, test, and deployment pipelines, environments, and secrets management.

  *   Cloud deployment of full-stack applications, including logging, monitoring, and deployment troubleshooting.



AI, Generative AI & Data Analytics for Engineers



  *   AI fundamentals: AI vs. Machine Learning vs. Deep Learning, supervised and unsupervised learning concepts, and industry use cases.

  *   LLMs & Generative AI: Working principles of LLMs, tokens, context, temperature, capabilities, limitations, and API integration.

  *   Prompt Engineering: Role-based prompting, context engineering, prompt patterns, structured outputs, and iterative prompt optimization.

  *   AI productivity tools: Effective use of GitHub Copilot/Claude for code generation, documentation, testing, refactoring, and analysis, including best practices and limitations.

  *   Building AI-powered applications: Introduction to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), chatbots, agents, and function calling.

  *   Responsible AI: AI output validation, hallucination and bias awareness, secure AI practices, data privacy, IP considerations, and organizational AI policies.

  *   Data Analytics: Advanced Excel, SQL for analytics, Power BI dashboards, and communicating business insights.



Capstone Project in Agile Mode



  *   Team-based capstone project (4–5 members) involving a full-stack application with a database, secured REST APIs, React frontend, an AI-powered feature, Docker, CI/CD, and cloud deployment.

  *   Two Scrum sprints covering backlog management, sprint planning, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.

  *   Engineering best practices including feature branching, pull requests, code reviews, testing, and documentation.

  *   Application hardening through UAT, bug fixing, performance and security checks, and release documentation.





Thanks & Regards,

Jyoti M

Based on the discussion with the client for the APM Experts (Aramco) requirement, please find the client's expectations below.

The client is not looking for a generic APM or SAP Asset Management trainer. They are specifically looking for a domain expert with strong Oil & Gas Asset Management experience, who can discuss business scenarios using industry-standard terminology and demonstrate a deep understanding of asset integrity and maintenance operations.

Client Expectations

*            Hands-on experience in Asset Performance Management (APM) within the Oil & Gas industry.

*            Strong understanding of Asset Integrity Management and maintenance best practices.

*            Ability to discuss industry-specific business processes using Oil & Gas terminology.

*            Experience explaining asset lifecycle management, inspection strategies, reliability, risk-based maintenance, and integrity management.

*            Ability to engage in functional discussions with client SMEs using real implementation examples rather than theoretical concepts.

*            Strong understanding of different asset maintenance functions, operational workflows, and business use cases within the Oil & Gas sector.

Key Feedback

During the assessment, the client was the trainer's domain expertise rather than product knowledge alone. They expect the trainer to confidently discuss Oil & Gas asset management concepts, industry practices, exceptions, operational scenarios, and integration points using the same terminology followed by Aramco and similar organizations.

### 2020. Passkeys by default a d  eti eme t of Mic osoft-p ovided SMS a d voice authe ticatio 

- Messages: 1
- Dates: 2026-08-12 02:29 IST ? 2026-08-12 02:29 IST

#### Message 1 ? 2026-08-12 02:29 IST

**From:** Microsoft <microsoft-noreply@microsoft.com>  
**To:** annapurna@clahantechnologies.com  
**Folder:** INBOX

Microsoft header logo

Move to phishing-resistant authentication before SMS and voice retire

=====================================================================



We are notifying all Microsoft Entra ID tenants of an important change to authentication security: The AI era demands stronger, phishing-resistant authentication. Passkeys are becoming the default authentication experience in Microsoft Entra, and Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication will retire on February 1, 2027. 



For more context on why Microsoft is moving to phishing-resistant authentication by default, please read our Microsoft Security Blog announcement. 



https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2026/07/13/microsoft-entra-id-security-updates-passkeys-are-the-default-authentication-method-in-entra-id/?msockid=370e7edffc796e4409a36893fd9e6fbb



** What is changing

-------------------

- Passkeys become the default authentication experience for users currently enabled for SMS or voice.



- Microsoft-provided telecom delivery for SMS and voice will be retired. Customer-managed telecom providers configured through the Microsoft Security Store are not affected.



** Why this is changing

-----------------------

SMS and voice are among the most vulnerable authentication methods available today and provide significantly weaker protection against phishing, SIM-swap, and replay attacks than passkeys. Moving to phishing-resistant methods gives your organization stronger security by default.



** Impact on you and key dates

------------------------------

- September 1, 2026 —Users enabled for SMS or voice are automatically enabled for passkeys and will be nudged to register a passkey when they next complete MFA. (If you do not want this, move users out of SMS or voice in the Authentication Methods Policy before this date.)



- February 1, 2027 —Microsoft-provided SMS and voice are fully retired in Microsoft Entra ID. Customer-managed telecom providers are unaffected.



- After February 1, 2027 — Users whose only available MFA method is SMS or voice will receive a blocking prompt to register a passkey before they can continue signing in. There is no opt out from this enforcement; it applies to all tenants.



If no users in your tenant are enabled for SMS or voice, no action is required and you can disregard the steps below. 



If you do have users enabled for SMS or voice, the required action is to move every one of those users off SMS and voice before February 1, 2027. Microsoft recommends passkeys — the default phishing-resistant credential in Microsoft Entra ID. Take the following steps:





1. Find affected users. Identify who in your tenant is still enabled for SMS or voice.



2. Move users to passkeys. Enable passkeys and run a registration campaign to drive adoption at scale before auto-enablement on September 1, 2026.



3. Communicate the change. Notify your users of what is changing, when, and the action they need to take.



4. Evaluate a telecom provider only if required. If you have a regulatory or operational need to keep SMS or voice, configure a customer-managed provider through the Microsoft Security Store before February 1, 2027 (provider options and pricing published beginning September 18, 2026; configuration available beginning October 30, 2026).



The bottom line: every SMS and voice user must be on a phishing-resistant method — passkeys are recommended — before Microsoft-provided SMS and voice retire on February 1, 2027. Acting before September 1, 2026 lets you move users on your own schedule and avoid blocking prompts.



Read migration guidance > >>

https://aka.ms/passkeybydefault



Privacy Statement

https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=521839



Microsoft Corporation, One Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052



Microsoft footer logo

Hi Murali and Annapurna 



 



Good morning, thank you for the support throughout. 



 



We are happy to confirm the below training program at Cencora. 



 



Hi Harish



 



Please share the PO with the team. Below are the details 



 





Program



Salesforce Training    





Dates



August 13th - September 18th (28th Aug & 14th Sep are holidays and the dates

might extend by a day or two in case of any additional holidays) 



1.	Timings : 10.0 AM - 7.00 PM    

2.	Training must be delivered ILT at Pune as per client norms.

3.	Training Address: 3rd Floor, Tower 4, Commerzone IT Park Internal

Rd, Commerzone IT Park, Yerawada, Pune, Maharashtra 411006

4.	POC: Samiha





Commercials



Rs.14,000 Per Day 



*Payment on successful completion of the program and sharing original

invoice or digitally signed copy. We will calculate 45 days from the date of

invoice received and the payment will be done accordingly.





 



Deliverables



 -Trainer should share any relevant inputs on use cases, scenarios,

reference material for the training in soft copy as before the training

starts. 



- Weekly/ Module end assessment is a mandate which should be in the form of

MCQ'S. MCQ'S should be shared prior 3 days prior the exam date.  



- Capstone project should be done before the end of the training 



-Training feedback to be good or above as per industry norms.





Travel and Stay Policy 



* TSE will take care of travel, accommodation, and food 



*	 En-route expenses: will be reimbursed on actuals. En-route expenses

will include only conveyance expense that is incurred on the way while

travelling between base location and destination like airport / railway

station and bus station - to place of stay. Supporting bill to be provided

for travel by cab. Without bill there will be no reimbursement.



Accommodation:



*	Stay and food will be included in the stay bill, and which will be

paid by TSE to Hotel (Bill to company)



Note : 



*      All bills need to be provided for claim; no claims will be

entertained without bills. 



*      Any additional cost needs to be borne by the consultant (Double

occupancy, Tips, Extra Dinner)



*      In case of any queries, you may reach your account manager.



	



 



Best Regards,



Anish Nyayapati

Dear Murali,



PFB the Meeting notes:





  *   Trainer Experience and Expertise Discussion: Naveen questioned Akshay about their background, experience in mobile device management, and specific expertise with Microsoft Intune and greenfield deployments, with Akshay providing a detailed overview of their skills and clarifying areas of limited experience.

     *   Trainer Background and Experience: Akshay described their decade-long career in mobile development, initially focusing on native Android, later expanding to iOS and cross-platform development, and working with major clients such as Invesco, Deloitte, and Kevin Tech.

     *   Device Management and Intune Expertise: Akshay explained their 5-6 years of experience in device management, including setting up and managing corporate and BYOD devices, handling certificate rotations, and working with Microsoft Intune for both Android and iOS platforms.

     *   Greenfield Deployment Experience: Naveen inquired about Akshay's experience with greenfield deployments and scratch-level configuration, to which Akshay clarified they have limited experience in this area and would not be able to provide in-depth training on building solutions from the ground up.

  *   Training Program Content and Structure Overview: Akshay presented the training program's Table of Contents (TOC), outlining modules on MDM installation, device management for Apple and Android, certificate management, Intune infrastructure, security, troubleshooting, and hands-on labs, with Naveen and Sripom Sinha seeking clarifications on specific inclusions.

     *   Modules and Topics Covered: Akshay detailed the training modules, including Apple ecosystem configuration, Android device management, app approvals, certificate and PKI management, Intune infrastructure, conditional access, mobile security operations, troubleshooting, log analysis, device lifecycle management, and reporting.

     *   Hands-On Labs and Requirements: Akshay confirmed that the training includes hands-on labs for all modules, requiring participants to have active Microsoft Intune access and physical devices for setup and testing, with experiential case studies such as device resets and certificate management.

     *   Apple Business Manager and Device Provisioning: Naveen asked if Apple Business Manager (ABM) would be covered, and Akshay confirmed its inclusion, noting that physical device provisioning may depend on feasibility and that further clarification would be provided in an official write-up.

     *   Certificate Management and Lab Provisioning: Naveen inquired about certificate training and provisioning, with Akshay stating that synthetic certificates would be issued for lab purposes and a separate document would clarify what is included in hands-on versus theoretical coverage.

  *   Clarifications on Training Scope and Exclusions: Sripom Sinha and Naveen asked Akshay about the inclusion of application package deployment, device migration, and lab device provisioning, with Akshay clarifying which topics are not included and promising an official document outlining responsibilities and requirements.

     *   Application Package Deployment: Sripom Sinha asked if the training would cover pushing application packages via company portal or store, and Akshay clarified that this is not included in the current training scope.

     *   Device and Application Migration: Sripom Sinha inquired about migration processes, such as moving 100 Android devices to Apple devices, and Akshay stated that only a single-device migration demonstration might be possible, with conceptual coverage not included in the TOC.

     *   Lab Device and Access Provisioning: Sripom Sinha asked about the provision of devices and access for labs, and Akshay clarified that participants must provide their own devices, with an official write-up to specify what is included from the training provider and what is required from participants.

  *   Certificate Expiry and Regeneration Process: Naveen and Akshay discussed the process for handling PKCS certificate expiry in Microsoft Intune, with Akshay explaining the impact on services and the automated regeneration process, and Naveen clarifying Intune's template-based handling.

     *   PKCS Certificate Expiry Handling: Akshay explained that when a PKCS certificate expires, services such as Wi-Fi, VPN, or email may fail, and the rotation process is initiated from the Intune PKCS profile, with temporary service disruption possible.

     *   Intune Template-Based Certificate Management: Naveen clarified that in Intune, PKCS certificates are managed via templates, and expiry is handled automatically without manual intervention, which Akshay acknowledged.

  *   Next Steps and Follow-Up Actions: Harshita requested Akshay to share a revised TOC and official documentation clarifying lab requirements and training inclusions, with Akshay agreeing to provide these materials after the call.

     *   Revised TOC and Documentation: Harshita asked Akshay to send a revised Table of Contents and a detailed write-up specifying what is included in the training and what support is needed from the client side, to which Akshay agreed.

Dear Murali,



PFB the Meeting notes:





  *   Trainer Experience and Expertise Discussion: Naveen questioned Akshay about their background, experience in mobile device management, and specific expertise with Microsoft Intune and greenfield deployments, with Akshay providing a detailed overview of their skills and clarifying areas of limited experience.

     *   Trainer Background and Experience: Akshay described their decade-long career in mobile development, initially focusing on native Android, later expanding to iOS and cross-platform development, and working with major clients such as Invesco, Deloitte, and Kevin Tech.

     *   Device Management and Intune Expertise: Akshay explained their 5-6 years of experience in device management, including setting up and managing corporate and BYOD devices, handling certificate rotations, and working with Microsoft Intune for both Android and iOS platforms.

     *   Greenfield Deployment Experience: Naveen inquired about Akshay's experience with greenfield deployments and scratch-level configuration, to which Akshay clarified they have limited experience in this area and would not be able to provide in-depth training on building solutions from the ground up.

  *   Training Program Content and Structure Overview: Akshay presented the training program's Table of Contents (TOC), outlining modules on MDM installation, device management for Apple and Android, certificate management, Intune infrastructure, security, troubleshooting, and hands-on labs, with Naveen and Sripom Sinha seeking clarifications on specific inclusions.

     *   Modules and Topics Covered: Akshay detailed the training modules, including Apple ecosystem configuration, Android device management, app approvals, certificate and PKI management, Intune infrastructure, conditional access, mobile security operations, troubleshooting, log analysis, device lifecycle management, and reporting.

     *   Hands-On Labs and Requirements: Akshay confirmed that the training includes hands-on labs for all modules, requiring participants to have active Microsoft Intune access and physical devices for setup and testing, with experiential case studies such as device resets and certificate management.

     *   Apple Business Manager and Device Provisioning: Naveen asked if Apple Business Manager (ABM) would be covered, and Akshay confirmed its inclusion, noting that physical device provisioning may depend on feasibility and that further clarification would be provided in an official write-up.

     *   Certificate Management and Lab Provisioning: Naveen inquired about certificate training and provisioning, with Akshay stating that synthetic certificates would be issued for lab purposes and a separate document would clarify what is included in hands-on versus theoretical coverage.

  *   Clarifications on Training Scope and Exclusions: Sripom Sinha and Naveen asked Akshay about the inclusion of application package deployment, device migration, and lab device provisioning, with Akshay clarifying which topics are not included and promising an official document outlining responsibilities and requirements.

     *   Application Package Deployment: Sripom Sinha asked if the training would cover pushing application packages via company portal or store, and Akshay clarified that this is not included in the current training scope.

     *   Device and Application Migration: Sripom Sinha inquired about migration processes, such as moving 100 Android devices to Apple devices, and Akshay stated that only a single-device migration demonstration might be possible, with conceptual coverage not included in the TOC.

     *   Lab Device and Access Provisioning: Sripom Sinha asked about the provision of devices and access for labs, and Akshay clarified that participants must provide their own devices, with an official write-up to specify what is included from the training provider and what is required from participants.

  *   Certificate Expiry and Regeneration Process: Naveen and Akshay discussed the process for handling PKCS certificate expiry in Microsoft Intune, with Akshay explaining the impact on services and the automated regeneration process, and Naveen clarifying Intune's template-based handling.

     *   PKCS Certificate Expiry Handling: Akshay explained that when a PKCS certificate expires, services such as Wi-Fi, VPN, or email may fail, and the rotation process is initiated from the Intune PKCS profile, with temporary service disruption possible.

     *   Intune Template-Based Certificate Management: Naveen clarified that in Intune, PKCS certificates are managed via templates, and expiry is handled automatically without manual intervention, which Akshay acknowledged.

  *   Next Steps and Follow-Up Actions: Harshita requested Akshay to share a revised TOC and official documentation clarifying lab requirements and training inclusions, with Akshay agreeing to provide these materials after the call.

     *   Revised TOC and Documentation: Harshita asked Akshay to send a revised Table of Contents and a detailed write-up specifying what is included in the training and what support is needed from the client side, to which Akshay agreed.

Dear Murali,



PFB the Meeting notes:





  *   Trainer Experience and Expertise Discussion: Naveen questioned Akshay about their background, experience in mobile device management, and specific expertise with Microsoft Intune and greenfield deployments, with Akshay providing a detailed overview of their skills and clarifying areas of limited experience.

     *   Trainer Background and Experience: Akshay described their decade-long career in mobile development, initially focusing on native Android, later expanding to iOS and cross-platform development, and working with major clients such as Invesco, Deloitte, and Kevin Tech.

     *   Device Management and Intune Expertise: Akshay explained their 5-6 years of experience in device management, including setting up and managing corporate and BYOD devices, handling certificate rotations, and working with Microsoft Intune for both Android and iOS platforms.

     *   Greenfield Deployment Experience: Naveen inquired about Akshay's experience with greenfield deployments and scratch-level configuration, to which Akshay clarified they have limited experience in this area and would not be able to provide in-depth training on building solutions from the ground up.

  *   Training Program Content and Structure Overview: Akshay presented the training program's Table of Contents (TOC), outlining modules on MDM installation, device management for Apple and Android, certificate management, Intune infrastructure, security, troubleshooting, and hands-on labs, with Naveen and Sripom Sinha seeking clarifications on specific inclusions.

     *   Modules and Topics Covered: Akshay detailed the training modules, including Apple ecosystem configuration, Android device management, app approvals, certificate and PKI management, Intune infrastructure, conditional access, mobile security operations, troubleshooting, log analysis, device lifecycle management, and reporting.

     *   Hands-On Labs and Requirements: Akshay confirmed that the training includes hands-on labs for all modules, requiring participants to have active Microsoft Intune access and physical devices for setup and testing, with experiential case studies such as device resets and certificate management.

     *   Apple Business Manager and Device Provisioning: Naveen asked if Apple Business Manager (ABM) would be covered, and Akshay confirmed its inclusion, noting that physical device provisioning may depend on feasibility and that further clarification would be provided in an official write-up.

     *   Certificate Management and Lab Provisioning: Naveen inquired about certificate training and provisioning, with Akshay stating that synthetic certificates would be issued for lab purposes and a separate document would clarify what is included in hands-on versus theoretical coverage.

  *   Clarifications on Training Scope and Exclusions: Sripom Sinha and Naveen asked Akshay about the inclusion of application package deployment, device migration, and lab device provisioning, with Akshay clarifying which topics are not included and promising an official document outlining responsibilities and requirements.

     *   Lab Device and Access Provisioning: Sripom Sinha asked about the provision of devices and access for labs, and Akshay clarified that participants must provide their own devices, with an official write-up to specify what is included from the training provider and what is required from participants.

  *   Certificate Expiry and Regeneration Process: Naveen and Akshay discussed the process for handling PKCS certificate expiry in Microsoft Intune, with Akshay explaining the impact on services and the automated regeneration process, and Naveen clarifying Intune's template-based handling.

     *   PKCS Certificate Expiry Handling: Akshay explained that when a PKCS certificate expires, services such as Wi-Fi, VPN, or email may fail, and the rotation process is initiated from the Intune PKCS profile, with temporary service disruption possible.

     *   Intune Template-Based Certificate Management: Naveen clarified that in Intune, PKCS certificates are managed via templates, and expiry is handled automatically without manual intervention, which Akshay acknowledged.

 Updates to OpenAI’s Privacy Policy


Hi Annapurna,

We’re updating our Privacy Policy to include information about ads in ChatGPT, including how they work and how you can control your experience.

Ads may appear on Free and Go plans. Plus, Pro, Enterprise, Business and Education plans do not have ads. Ads do not influence the answers ChatGPT gives you. When you see an ad, it is always clearly labeled as an ad and is visually separated from the organic answer. You’ll get relevant and personalized ads using information that stays only on ChatGPT, such as ads you've interacted with, or context from your chats. You can manage ad personalization anytime in settings.

Your personal details and conversations with ChatGPT are private and are not shared with advertisers. Advertisers do not have access to your chats, chat history, memories, or personal details. Advertisers only receive overall information about how their ads perform, such as total views or clicks.

Learn more about ads in ChatGPT and our privacy controls, including how we protect your data.

Thanks,

The OpenAI Team

( https://www.athiya.com )



( https://www.linkedin.com/company/athiya-global ) ­

NEWSLETTER - JULY,  2026



*VOICE OF ATHIYA*



A Talent, Learning and AI Solutions Company



Image generated using AI



*Welcome to the Era of Human + Digital Teams*

---------------------------------------------



Last year, if you joined a Teams meeting, you were greeted by names like Raj, Anita, Sarah and John.



Today, there's a good chance another participant has quietly joined the meeting too.



Copilot.



Gemini.



Fireflies.ai.



Or an AI agent patiently taking notes, capturing action items and preparing the meeting summary before someone has even remembered to hit "Record."



Let's be honest... that colleague is probably the most punctual person on the call.



Welcome to the era of Human + Digital Teams.



According to Gartner, by 2028, one in three enterprise software applications will include agentic AI, while Microsoft's latest Work Trend Index suggests business leaders increasingly expect AI agents to become part of everyday work. Digital colleagues are no longer a futuristic concept—they're quietly becoming part of the organizational chart.



The interesting question isn't whether AI will join our teams.



It's how we'll manage teams where some colleagues happen to be algorithms.



Because unlike human colleagues, AI doesn't instinctively know what's confidential, when context matters, or that "please don't send this to the client yet" is usually an important instruction.



Without clear guardrails, an employee could unknowingly upload confidential client proposals into a public AI tool, rely on an AI-generated market analysis containing fabricated references, or use AI to draft performance feedback that unintentionally reflects bias. None of these mistakes begin with bad intent. They begin with good intentions and no governance.



Which is why we're seeing a new leadership priority emerge—not just AI adoption, but AI governance.



Organizations are beginning to ask questions that didn't exist two years ago.



Should every employee have access to every AI tool?



Which AI platforms are approved?



Who reviews AI-generated client content before it leaves the organization?



Should AI be allowed to make recommendations on hiring, promotions or performance reviews?



Those aren't technology decisions.



They're business decisions.



At Athiya, we've noticed that our own project teams have quietly evolved. Today, a typical learning project isn't built by just programme managers, instructional designers, facilitators and moderators.



There's usually an AI teammate somewhere in the mix.



One helps our instructional designers brainstorm learning journeys. Another summarizes research. A third prototypes activities. Yet another challenges our first draft (sometimes quite confidently... and occasionally quite incorrectly).



The difference is that we've built human checkpoints into every stage. Every AI output is reviewed, challenged and refined by experts. We also follow internal guardrails around confidentiality, client data, prompt practices and responsible AI use, ensuring our human expertise remains firmly in the driver's seat while AI does what it does best—accelerate the journey.



So yes, our project teams have grown.



Not because we've hired more people.



Because we've learned how to combine human judgment with digital capability.



Perhaps that's the real workplace transformation.



The future won't belong to organizations with the most AI.



It will belong to those that build the best Human + Digital Teams.



*July Highlights:*



* July saw Athiya deliver a series of highly interactive, gamified in-person workshops for managers, equipping them with practical strategies to navigate increasingly complex business environments, make better decisions and lead confidently through change.



* Across industries, Athiya partnered with clients to deliver diverse learning experiences spanning AI adoption, AI literacy and behavioural capability building, helping professionals strengthen both the technical and human skills needed in today's workplace.



* Through Athiya IDA (Intelligent. Diverse. Adaptive.), our research and innovation team continued exploring new ways of integrating AI into programme design and learning experiences. From accelerating content development to enhancing learner engagement, the team is experimenting with AI as a collaborative partner—always guided by human expertise, quality assurance and responsible AI practices.



*Did you know?*



London taxi drivers develop a larger hippocampus, the part of the brain linked to memory, after years of navigating the city's 25,000+ streets without GPS.



Looks like "learning by doing" really does leave its mark. 🚖🧠



Source: University College London (Eleanor Maguire's famous The Knowledge study)



­



*New Playlist: Athiya's Quick Behavioural Tips*



­



W e're excited to share this new playlist of 1-minute quick behavioural tips with anyone who might need them. Starting with the first video on the hidden cost of constant task switching.



The hidden cost of constant task switching video ( https://youtu.be/x1sVx9Pa-pM )

An updated Priority Community Support experience begins 20 August 2026

You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that recently used technical support in the last 90 days and may be eligible for the updated Priority Community Support experience. Beginning today, 20 August 2026, we'll introduce an updated Priority Community Support experience for eligible customers. As part of the enhanced workflow, when you create a support request through the Azure portal, a support ticket is automatically generated to ensure your issue is tracked from the start. An AI-powered support agent will first work with you to understand the issue and recommend potential solutions. If the AI agent is unable to resolve the issue, you will be guided back to the Azure portal, where a Microsoft Q&A post will be automatically prepared on your behalf to enable a seamless transition to Priority Community Support. 


What to expect


The updated experience is designed to:


Get faster resolution through AI-assisted troubleshooting and streamlined support workflows.


Reduce the need to re-enter information when moving between support resources.


Preserve relevant troubleshooting history to help support experts understand what you've already tried.


Help route your request to the appropriate support resource.


Continue receiving one-on-one support engineering assistance when your scenario requires direct engagement with Microsoft Support.


This enhanced experience reduces repetitive work, improves tracking, and helps connect you with the right support resources more quickly.


Customer data, security, and privacy continue to be protected. Personally identifiable information (PII) and company-specific information are automatically removed before the post is created. If sensitive information is required, it will be collected through secure, private channels rather than public forums.


No action is required. If your subscription is eligible, the updated experience will become available automatically beginning 20 August 2026.


Help and support


To learn more about Priority Community Support (PCS), including how questions are handled and how privacy is maintained, review the Priority Community Support documentation. If you have questions or feedback regarding this change, contact pcsquestions@service.microsoft.com.

Cloud Computing & DevOps



  *   Cloud concepts: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, regions & availability zones, shared responsibility model, and pricing awareness.

  *   Core cloud services (AWS or Azure based on demand): Compute (EC2/App Service), Storage (S3/Blob), Networking (VPC/VNet, Security Groups), and Managed Databases.

  *   Docker: Images, containers, Dockerfile, Docker Compose, and containerizing a full-stack application.

  *   CI/CD using GitHub Actions: Build, test, and deployment pipelines, environments, and secrets management.

  *   Cloud deployment of full-stack applications, including logging, monitoring, and deployment troubleshooting.



AI, Generative AI & Data Analytics for Engineers



  *   AI fundamentals: AI vs. Machine Learning vs. Deep Learning, supervised and unsupervised learning concepts, and industry use cases.

  *   LLMs & Generative AI: Working principles of LLMs, tokens, context, temperature, capabilities, limitations, and API integration.

  *   Prompt Engineering: Role-based prompting, context engineering, prompt patterns, structured outputs, and iterative prompt optimization.

  *   AI productivity tools: Effective use of GitHub Copilot/Claude for code generation, documentation, testing, refactoring, and analysis, including best practices and limitations.

  *   Building AI-powered applications: Introduction to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), chatbots, agents, and function calling.

  *   Responsible AI: AI output validation, hallucination and bias awareness, secure AI practices, data privacy, IP considerations, and organizational AI policies.

  *   Data Analytics: Advanced Excel, SQL for analytics, Power BI dashboards, and communicating business insights.



Capstone Project in Agile Mode



  *   Team-based capstone project (4–5 members) involving a full-stack application with a database, secured REST APIs, React frontend, an AI-powered feature, Docker, CI/CD, and cloud deployment.

  *   Two Scrum sprints covering backlog management, sprint planning, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.

  *   Engineering best practices including feature branching, pull requests, code reviews, testing, and documentation.

  *   Application hardening through UAT, bug fixing, performance and security checks, and release documentation.

Dear Michel,

I am really sorry to write this email, and I would like to sincerely thank you for your support and contributions to the organization.

Your last working day with the organization will be 10 September 2026.

I was waiting and hoping that at least one of the projects we were pursuing would get approved so that we could secure the required funding and continue operations smoothly. Unfortunately, despite our efforts and waiting for the past several months, nothing has progressed in the direction we expected.

I sincerely apologize for having to take this decision. At present, I am facing a significant shortage of funds to continue running the business. For the last six months, we have not been able to generate sufficient revenue, and the current financial situation has made it extremely difficult for me to sustain the operations.

I hope you will understand the situation and the circumstances behind this decision. This is not a decision I have taken easily, and I genuinely appreciate your patience, understanding, and contribution during this period.

Before your last working day, I request you to complete a proper handover of all the responsibilities and operational information to Swarupa, including:

Employee database and related information

Login credentials and access details

GST-related information and records

Accounts and financial-related information

Company documents and records

Ongoing operational activities

Any pending tasks, projects, or follow-ups

Other day-to-day operational responsibilities and information required for a smooth transition

Please ensure that all relevant information, documents, credentials, and responsibilities are properly handed over to Swarupa before your last working day.

Once again, I sincerely apologize for the situation and thank you for your understanding and support. I wish you all the very best in your future endeavors, and I genuinely hope we can remain on good terms moving forward.

Regards,

Explore the small business plugins that help your business run smoother in ChatGPT

Meet the Small Business Collection in ChatGPT

Explore a collection of plugins and skills built for small businesses. Connect your everyday tools, bring in your business context, and let ChatGPT take work off your plate.

One of the most common questions we hear from small business owners is: “How can ChatGPT understand more of my business and help me get more done?” Most businesses run on software across marketing, HR, finance, and more, which means flipping through tabs to keep the business moving.

The small business collection makes it easy to connect your tools to ChatGPT through plugins. Think of plugins as a tool belt: each gives ChatGPT the context and capabilities for a specific job, so ChatGPT Work can take on that work for you.

 Explore the collection

Here’s how to get started:

Step 1: Install plugins you already use every day.

Step 2: Try a prompt in ChatGPT Work to get started.

Prioritize today’s sales follow-ups with @HubSpot

Find overdue invoices to collect on with @QuickBooks

Spot surprises before payday with @Gusto

Create an on-brand Instagram post with @Canva

Pro tip: Plugins work best in ChatGPT Work, which is available to all plans on desktop, and to Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu on web and mobile.

Step 3: Review and refine.

Always check your results, iterate, and review proposed actions before approving them.

Plugins will respect your existing account permissions and workspace controls. Learn more about how plugins work in the help center article.

Discover the 16 plugins in the Small Business Collection

Browse the full collection, install a plugin, and ask ChatGPT Work to take something off your plate.

 Explore the collection

Want to receive more updates like this? Sign up for our small business newsletter.

Plugin availability, terms & privacy

Plugin availability and features vary by plan, region, and workspace settings, and a connected third-party account may be required. Use is subject to OpenAI’s terms and the connected services’ terms and privacy policies; relevant information from your conversation may be shared with those services to fulfill your requests. OpenAI does not use ChatGPT Business workspace data to train its models by default; see each plugin’s listing for connection requirements and third-party privacy details.

### 2130. The sma te  AI gets, the sma te  huma s  eed to be

NEWSLETTER - AUGUST,  2026



*VOICE OF ATHIYA*



A Talent, Learning and AI Solutions Company



Image generated using AI



*The Smarter AI Gets, the Smarter Humans Need to Be*

----------------------------------------------------



Every technological revolution arrives with a familiar prediction: "Training won't be needed anymore." We heard it when computers entered offices, when Google put knowledge in everyone's pocket and again when online learning became mainstream.



Yet here we are.



The AI era is no different. If anything, it has made learning more important than ever.



According to the World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025, 39% of today's core workplace skills are expected to change by 2030. That's not a reason to reduce learning budgets. It's a reason to redesign them.



The smartest organizations have already figured this out.



Retail giant Walmart has invested over US$1 billion in employee learning while expanding AI capabilities across the business. DBS Bank has trained its entire workforce in AI fundamentals—not because everyone needs to become a data scientist, but because everyone needs to understand how AI is changing work. Even IKEA has used AI as an opportunity to reskill employees into higher-value customer-facing roles rather than simply automate routine work.



Somewhere along the way, many organizations assumed that if AI could answer questions, employees no longer needed to learn.



That's a bit like buying a piano and assuming everyone in the house can now play Mozart.



AI has certainly become the fastest colleague in the room. It drafts reports before you've finished your coffee, builds presentations in minutes and somehow manages to sound remarkably confident about almost everything.



Including the things it occasionally gets spectacularly wrong.



This is exactly why Human-in-the-Loop has become one of the most important principles in AI adoption. AI can analyse, recommend and generate. Humans must still question, interpret and decide.



Ironically, many organizations are investing heavily in smarter AI while forgetting to invest in smarter humans.



If AI drafts the proposal, people still need the judgment to know whether it should be sent.



If AI recommends the best candidate, leaders still need empathy and ethics to make the hiring decision.



If AI predicts the next business opportunity, executives still need strategic thinking to decide whether it's the right one.



AI doesn't reduce the need for behavioural capability.



It raises the standard for it.



Critical thinking, communication, leadership, influence, collaboration and ethical decision-making are no longer "soft skills." They are the skills that determine whether AI becomes a multiplier—or a very expensive mistake.



At Athiya, this is exactly why we've reimagined many of our learning journeys. AI literacy is no longer taught in isolation. It is woven together with behavioural capability, practical application and responsible AI adoption because successful transformation isn't just about teaching people how to use AI.



It's about preparing them to work confidently alongside it.



Perhaps the biggest misconception of the AI era is that technology will reduce the need for human development.



The opposite is happening.



The smarter AI becomes, the smarter humans need to become.



*August Highlights:*



* August marked an exciting milestone as Athiya partnered with a new client to deliver a senior leadership development programme. The highly interactive workshops received an enthusiastic response, reinforcing our belief that today's leaders need practical strategies to navigate complexity, inspire teams and lead through constant change.

* Our AI adoption journey gathered further momentum, with a series of AI literacy and AI adoption workshops successfully delivered across multiple client organizations. From responsible AI usage to integrating AI into everyday work, the programmes equipped professionals with the confidence to move from curiosity to practical application.

* Through Athiya IDA (Intelligent. Diverse. Adaptive.), our research and innovation team continued advancing AI-enabled learning design by exploring new approaches to programme development, learner engagement and digital facilitation. Every innovation remains grounded in responsible AI practices, with human expertise ensuring quality, creativity and meaningful learning outcomes.



*Did you know?*



The brain doesn't distinguish particularly well between an event you vividly imagine and one you actually experience. That's why elite athletes mentally rehearse before competitions.



Looks like your brain has been running "practice mode" all along. 🏅🧠



Source: Sports psychology research by Richard Suinn



­

Hi Team,



Greetings from SkillsGain!

We have an upcoming long-term Agentic AI / Generative AI Technical Training engagement and wanted to check your interest and availability.

Program Overview



  *   Duration: 8 weeks per batch

  *   October Batch: Tentatively starting from mid-October

  *   Engagement: Initially, the trainer will shadow the existing October batch to understand the curriculum, delivery methodology, exercises, projects, and participant expectations.

  *   From the subsequent batch onwards, the trainer will be expected to independently deliver the complete program end-to-end.

  *   We are expecting approximately 4 subsequent batches over the coming year, so preference is for a trainer who can commit to a longer-term engagement.



Technical Expertise Required

We are specifically looking for a hands-on technical practitioner/trainer, not only a GenAI facilitator.

The trainer should have practical experience in areas such as:



  *   Agentic AI & AI Agents

  *   Generative AI / LLM applications

  *   Agent development and orchestration

  *   Tool Calling / Function Calling

  *   API integration

  *   RAG

  *   Agent Memory & Context Management

  *   Multi-Agent Systems

  *   Planner–Solver / Critic–Executor patterns

  *   Agent evaluation and evaluation frameworks

  *   Production deployment of GenAI/Agentic AI applications

  *   Observability, monitoring, security and reliability

  *   Python and hands-on implementation

  *   LangChain / LangGraph or similar frameworks



The specific framework is not mandatory. Strong practical Agentic AI experience is more important.

Delivery Schedule



  *   Monday–Thursday: 2 hours/day

  *   Friday: 4 hours/day

  *   Sessions will generally start around 10:00 AM

  *   Friday will be a practical war-room/application session, involving hands-on problem solving, implementation and project discussions.



Delivery Model

The cohort will be hybrid, with participants across Bangalore, Pune and Gurugram.

Location preference:



  1.  Bangalore

  2.  Pune



The trainer should be comfortable supporting the hybrid model and the required in-person engagement.

Commercials

Our target budget is approximately ₹3,000/hour.

Initial Screening

Could you please share the following details?



  1.  Current designation

  2.  Total experience

  3.  Relevant Agentic AI / GenAI experience

  4.  Examples of Agentic AI systems/projects you have personally built or worked on

  5.  Experience with RAG, tool/function calling, memory and multi-agent workflows

  6.  Experience with Agent/LLM evaluation

  7.  Production deployment experience, if any

  8.  Technical training experience and audience handled

  9.  Current location

  10. Availability for the October batch

  11. Availability for subsequent batches

  12. Expected hourly commercial

  13. Willingness to commit to the October shadowing + approximately 4 subsequent batches



If the profile appears suitable, we will schedule a 10–15 minute technical validation call with you before sharing your profile with the client.

Please share your updated profile/CV along with the above details.

Thanks & Regards,

Subject: Agentic AI / Generative AI Technical Training requirement - Bangalore



Hi Team,



Greetings from SkillsGain!

We have an upcoming long-term Agentic AI / Generative AI Technical Training engagement and wanted to check your interest and availability.

Program Overview



  *   Duration: 8 weeks per batch

  *   October Batch: Tentatively starting from mid-October

  *   Engagement: Initially, the trainer will shadow the existing October batch to understand the curriculum, delivery methodology, exercises, projects, and participant expectations.

  *   From the subsequent batch onwards, the trainer will be expected to independently deliver the complete program end-to-end.

  *   We are expecting approximately 4 subsequent batches over the coming year, so preference is for a trainer who can commit to a longer-term engagement.



Technical Expertise Required

We are specifically looking for a hands-on technical practitioner/trainer, not only a GenAI facilitator.

The trainer should have practical experience in areas such as:



  *   Agentic AI & AI Agents

  *   Generative AI / LLM applications

  *   Agent development and orchestration

  *   Tool Calling / Function Calling

  *   API integration

  *   RAG

  *   Agent Memory & Context Management

  *   Multi-Agent Systems

  *   Planner–Solver / Critic–Executor patterns

  *   Agent evaluation and evaluation frameworks

  *   Production deployment of GenAI/Agentic AI applications

  *   Observability, monitoring, security and reliability

  *   Python and hands-on implementation

  *   LangChain / LangGraph or similar frameworks



The specific framework is not mandatory. Strong practical Agentic AI experience is more important.

Delivery Schedule



  *   Monday–Thursday: 2 hours/day

  *   Friday: 4 hours/day

  *   Sessions will generally start around 10:00 AM

  *   Friday will be a practical war-room/application session, involving hands-on problem solving, implementation and project discussions.



Delivery Model

The cohort will be hybrid, with participants across Bangalore, Pune and Gurugram.

Location preference:



  1.  Bangalore

  2.  Pune



The trainer should be comfortable supporting the hybrid model and the required in-person engagement.

Commercials

Our target budget is approximately ₹3,000/hour.

Initial Screening

Could you please share the following details?



  1.  Current designation

  2.  Total experience

  3.  Relevant Agentic AI / GenAI experience

  4.  Examples of Agentic AI systems/projects you have personally built or worked on

  5.  Experience with RAG, tool/function calling, memory and multi-agent workflows

  6.  Experience with Agent/LLM evaluation

  7.  Production deployment experience, if any

  8.  Technical training experience and audience handled

  9.  Current location

  10. Availability for the October batch

  11. Availability for subsequent batches

  12. Expected hourly commercial

  13. Willingness to commit to the October shadowing + approximately 4 subsequent batches



If the profile appears suitable, we will schedule a 10–15 minute technical validation call with you before sharing your profile with the client.

Please share your updated profile/CV along with the above details.

Thanks & Regards,

Hi Tapan,



Greetings of the day!



As discussed over the call, we have an upcoming long-term Agentic AI / 

Generative AI Technical Training engagement, and we would like to check 

your interest and availability for the same.



Program Overview



	*



Duration: 8 weeks per batch

	*



October Batch: Tentatively starting from mid-October

	*



Engagement: Initially, the trainer will shadow the existing October 

batch to understand the curriculum, delivery methodology, exercises, 

projects, and participant expectations.

	*



 From the subsequent batch onwards, the trainer will be expected to 

independently deliver the complete program end-to-end.

	*



We are expecting approximately 4 subsequent batches over the coming 

year, so preference will be given to a trainer who can commit to a 

longer-term engagement.



Technical Expertise Required



We are specifically looking for a hands-on technical 

practitioner/trainer, rather than only a GenAI facilitator.



The trainer should have practical experience in areas such as:



	*



Agentic AI & AI Agents

	*



Generative AI / LLM applications

	*



Agent development and orchestration

	*



Tool Calling / Function Calling

	*



API integration

	*



RAG

	*



Agent Memory & Context Management

	*



Multi-Agent Systems

	*



Planner-Solver / Critic-Executor patterns

	*



Agent evaluation and evaluation frameworks

	*



Production deployment of GenAI/Agentic AI applications

	*



Observability, monitoring, security, and reliability

	*



Python and hands-on implementation

	*



LangChain / LangGraph or similar frameworks



The specific framework is not mandatory. Strong practical experience in 

Agentic AI is more important.



Delivery Schedule



	*



Monday-Thursday: 2 hours/day

	*



Friday: 4 hours/day

	*



Sessions will generally start around 10:00 AM

	*



Friday will be a practical war-room/application session, involving 

hands-on problem-solving, implementation, and project discussions.



Delivery Model



The cohort will be hybrid, with participants based in Bangalore.



Location Preference: Bangalore



The trainer should be comfortable supporting the hybrid delivery model 

and the required in-person engagement.



Commercials: 2K per hour & not included t&a.



Initial Screening



Could you please share the following details?



	*



Current designation

	*



Total experience

	*



Relevant Agentic AI / GenAI experience

	*



Examples of Agentic AI systems/projects you have personally built or 

worked on

	*



Experience with RAG, tool/function calling, memory, and multi-agent 

workflows

	*



Experience with Agent/LLM evaluation

	*



Production deployment experience, if any

	*



Technical training experience and the audiences handled

	*



Current location

	*



Availability for the October batch

	*



Availability for subsequent batches

	*



Willingness to commit to the October shadowing + approximately 4 

subsequent batches



Please acknowledge the email and confirm your interest and availability.



Thanks & Regards,

Annapurna U.

Hi Akshay,

Please find below the client’s requirements for the upcoming 4-day training. The client has requested the final curriculum along with the technical requirements for the training.

Please find below the Sample Dashboard Requirements

1. Dynamic Date Parameters



The dashboard allows users to define the analysis period through configurable Start Date and End Date parameters.



Users can therefore analyse any required period without needing separate dashboards or predefined date filters.



Example:



  *   Start Date ? 01/09/2026

  *   End Date ? 30/09/2026



All KPIs, charts and tables dynamically update based on the selected period.



________________________________

2. Flexible Comparison Period



A dedicated Comparison Period parameter allows users to select how the current period should be compared.



For example:



  *   Day-to-Day / Same Period Last Year

  *   Custom Comparison Period



When Day-to-Day Last Year is selected, the dashboard automatically derives the corresponding previous-year dates.



When the user switches to Custom Comparison, the dashboard dynamically displays separate Comparison Start Date and Comparison End Date parameters.



This was implemented using Tableau parameter actions + Control Visibility, so the user interface changes based on the selected comparison methodology.



This allows the same dashboard to support:



Current Period

? 01/09/2026 – 30/09/2026



vs.



Previous Year

? 01/09/2025 – 30/09/2025



or



Custom Comparison

? User-defined start and end dates.



________________________________

3. Dynamic Growth & Variance Calculations



Once the comparison period is selected, the dashboard dynamically calculates:



  *   Growth %

  *   Growth value

  *   Share

  *   Margin change

  *   Quantity growth

  *   Digital share movement

  *   Other relevant business KPIs



The same comparison logic is propagated across the different visualisations, ensuring that users don’t have to manually calculate or interpret the variance.



________________________________

4. Dynamic Granularity



The dashboard supports changing the level of analysis/granularity without requiring separate worksheets or dashboards.



Users can move between different levels such as:



Country ? State ? City/Cluster ? Store



or other relevant business hierarchies.



This allows the same visualisation to answer both high-level management questions and detailed operational questions.



________________________________

5. Dynamic Table Sorting



Tables are designed with interactive sorting capabilities.



Users can sort ascending or descending based on any of the key metrics available in the table, such as:



  *   Turnover

  *   Growth %

  *   Turnover Share

  *   Quantity

  *   Quantity Growth

  *   Digital Share

  *   Margin

  *   Margin Growth



This allows users to quickly identify:



Top performers ? Bottom performers ? Fastest growing ? Largest declines



without having to create separate versions of the table.



________________________________

6. Dynamic KPI Cards



The dashboard provides an executive-level KPI layer showing metrics such as:



  *   Turnover

  *   Digital Turnover

  *   Quantity

  *   Margin

  *   Average Basket Value

  *   Average Basket Quantity

  *   Average Selling Price

  *   Digital Share



Each KPI can display the current value alongside its comparison/growth, making performance changes immediately visible.



________________________________

7. Channel-Level Performance



The dashboard provides a breakdown of performance across different sales channels, enabling users to understand the contribution from:



  *   Physical / In-store

  *   Online

  *   B2B

  *   Marketplace

  *   Other relevant channels



This provides a consolidated view of both physical and digital business performance.



________________________________

8. Interactive Trend Analysis



Users can analyse performance trends over time with configurable:



  *   Metric selection

  *   Time granularity

  *   Current vs previous-period comparison

  *   Month-level or other time-level analysis



This makes it possible to move from a single KPI snapshot into understanding how performance has evolved over time.



________________________________

9. Business Dimension Filtering



The dashboard supports interactive filtering across relevant business dimensions such as:



  *   Geography

  *   City / Cluster

  *   State

  *   Sport / Category

  *   Store

  *   Channel

  *   Other business hierarchies



The filters are applied consistently across the dashboard to maintain a connected analytical experience.



________________________________

10. Drill-Down & Deep-Dive Analysis



The dashboard is structured so that users can move from:



Executive Overview ? Business Dimension ? Detailed Performance



This allows stakeholders to identify an issue at the summary level and then drill down to understand where the change is coming from.



________________________________

11. User-Controlled Dashboard Experience



Rather than creating multiple dashboards for different analytical requirements, several elements are controlled dynamically through Tableau parameters, calculated fields and dashboard actions.



Examples include:



  *   Dynamic date selection

  *   Dynamic comparison methodology

  *   Conditional parameter visibility

  *   Dynamic granularity

  *   Dynamic metric selection

  *   Interactive sorting

  *   Drill-down

  *   Contextual filtering



This creates a single self-service analytical dashboard that can support multiple business use cases.

A successful pilot can demonstrate what AI is capable of. 



Scaling that success across the organisation requires a different approach. 



Moving from proof of concept to sustained AI investment introduces new questions around the business case, financial considerations, risk, governance and executive sponsorship. 



In the first session of From Pilot to Production, we’ll explore what it actually takes to make that transition. 



We’ll examine:



•                                                                                            How to build a business case for ongoing AI investment



•                                                                                The financial, risk and governance questions to address



•                                                                    What changes when moving from project to sustained investment

Dear Team,



We are excited to announce the launch of our very first training program -

ITIL 5 AI Governance Certification, scheduled for November 14 and 15, from

10:30 AM to 5:30 PM.



As Artificial Intelligence continues to transform the workplace,

understanding how to use AI responsibly, securely, and effectively is

becoming an essential professional skill. AI governance is no longer just a

compliance consideration; it is a critical capability for organizations and

employees navigating an AI-driven future.



Why Is AI Governance Important?



*	Manage AI Risks Effectively: Understand potential risks related to

data privacy, security, bias, and unreliable AI outputs before they impact

business operations.

*	Ensure Responsible AI Adoption: Learn how governance frameworks help

promote ethical, transparent, accountable, and trustworthy AI usage.

*	Stay Ahead of Evolving Regulations: Build awareness of emerging AI

governance requirements and the importance of aligning AI practices with

organizational policies and applicable regulations.

*	Strengthen Your Professional Edge: Gain structured knowledge and a

certification that can help demonstrate your commitment to responsible AI

adoption and support your career growth in an increasingly AI-driven

business environment.



As AI becomes more deeply integrated into everyday workflows, employees who

understand AI governance will be better equipped to make informed decisions,

identify risks, and contribute to responsible innovation. Investing in AI

governance knowledge today can help individuals and organizations stay

prepared for tomorrow's challenges.



What Does the Program Include?



The two-day program is designed to provide an engaging, practical learning

experience, including:



*	2 days of live, interactive online sessions

*	Certification exam voucher

NEWSLETTER - SEPTEMBER,  2026



*VOICE OF ATHIYA*



A Talent, Learning and AI Solutions Company



*India Went Digital. Why Is Corporate Learning Still Waiting?*

--------------------------------------------------------------



India can make payments in seconds, order groceries in minutes, and binge-watch an entire series over a weekend.



But corporate learning? Sometimes we're still waiting for the next workshop invitation.



To be fair, we've made progress. Organizations have invested in platforms like LinkedIn Learning and Coursera, giving employees access to thousands of courses.



Wonderful! But having 10,000 courses available doesn't automatically mean 10,000 learning opportunities translate into better workplace performance.



A course subscription is not a learning strategy. (Although it certainly looks impressive on a dashboard.)



Here's something interesting.



Emeritus's 2025 Global Workplace Skills Study found that 79% of Indian learners prefer hybrid learning, compared with 67% globally.



Clearly, learners are ready for something more.



Imagine a leadership workshop followed by short digital scenarios, personalized practice, manager check-ins, and timely learning nudges.



Or onboarding that recognizes what employees already know, rather than making everyone complete the same 45 slides. Including the person who helped write them.



That's the real opportunity for digital learning.



At Athiya, we believe great learning doesn't have to choose between human interaction and technology. Thoughtfully designed blended experiences can bring together the best of both, making learning more engaging, relevant, and measurable.



India has embraced digital transformation with remarkable enthusiasm.



Perhaps it's time corporate learning joined the party.



Because the goal isn't to get employees to complete more courses. It's to help them do their jobs better.



And preferably without another 60-slide presentation.



*September Highlights:*



­



*1. Launching Careers, Building Confidence*



Athiya successfully delivered engaging, in-person training workshops for newly hired university graduates, helping them make a confident transition from campus to corporate life. These interactive sessions focused on strengthening workplace communication, professional skills, collaboration, and readiness for their career journeys.



*2. Accelerating AI Adoption*



Athiya's AI vertical, IDA (Intelligent • Diverse • Adaptive), delivered practical AI adoption workshops, helping professionals move beyond AI awareness to real-world application. The sessions focused on building AI confidence, exploring workplace use cases, and encouraging responsible and effective AI adoption.



­



*Looking Ahead: October 💡*



*Digital Learning Takes Center Stage!*



This October, Athiya is launching a dedicated digital learning and eLearning campaign to showcase our deep expertise in designing engaging, customized, and impactful learning experiences. Through fresh insights, creative showcases, and practical examples, we'll demonstrate how thoughtfully designed digital learning can help organizations build capabilities, improve learner engagement, and drive measurable outcomes.



Follow us on LinkedIn ( https://www.linkedin.com/company/athiya-organizational-competencies/?viewAsMember=true ) to stay tuned! We're excited to show you what great digital learning can look like.



­

The business case may be approved.



But successful AI deployment depends on whether your organisation is ready to adopt and sustain the change.



In the second session of From Pilot to Production, we’ll explore what it takes to prepare leaders, managers and frontline teams for AI-driven change, and how organisations can build adoption that lasts beyond go-live.

We’ll examine:



•                                                                                            How to assess organisational readiness



•                                                                                What successful AI change programmes get right



•                                                                    How to build adoption and sustain momentum



Because successful AI adoption doesn’t happen at go-live. It happens when people are ready to make the change stick.
